free_tier.stated:
Users now have a limit of 200GB for private models and 200GB for private datasets.

Kaggle has also doubled the maximum upload size of public models and datasets from 100GB to 200GB.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: maximum upload size of public models and datasets is 200GB; private models have a limit of 200GB
per_object_cap.notes: Kaggle has also doubled the maximum upload size of public models and datasets from 100GB to 200GB.

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: unverified: the models documentation and quota announcement state no retention period

egress.terms: Free. Files come from Kaggle's Google-hosted CDN (storage.googleapis.com) with no egress meter. Downloads require a Kaggle API token.

interface_detail: Many developers will need to download models in code outside of Kaggle. There are a few different methods: via the [kagglehub Python library](https://github.com/Kaggle/kagglehub), via our [Kaggle CLI](https://github.com/Kaggle/kaggle-cli), or by calling the API directly.
tooling: kagglehub and the Kaggle API. Verified live this session: GET /api/v1/models/list?search=bert and ?search=qwen both returned 200 with real model records (ref, title, author, vote counts); GET /api/v1/models/google/bert/get returned 200, 72,158 bytes. Datasets: /api/v1/datasets/list returns 200 JSON with totalBytesNullable per dataset. Note the upload side is narrower than the read side — 'The ability to upload models via the Kaggle API was introduced to a select group of Kaggle accounts starting in version 1.5.18', and kagglehub caps at 50 files per repo and auto-zips beyond that.
chaining: This tool allows you to copy model versions from one model to another. You can import versions from any public model or private models where you have collaborator access.

limits.value: maximum upload size of public models and datasets is 200GB; private models have a limit of 200GB

limits_note: Per-object-cap 200 GB and 50 top-level files per dataset. 'A max of 50 top-level files (if you have more, use a directory structure and upload an archive)'. Uploading via the API is write-gated for most accounts. Practical caveat from the docs: archives are uncompressed server-side so their contents are usable in Notebooks, which means the 200 GB is measured on the expanded tree.
reliability_note: Kaggle is Google-owned and long-lived; the risk is policy drift on public storage, not disappearance. The 200 GB private pool is enforced hard ('if you exceed this, either make your datasets public or delete unused datasets').
confidence_note: The Kaggle product announcement was read on 2026-11-09 and states the private and public model and dataset size limits.

extras.verified_at_basis: checked against the live service on 2026-11-09
extras.quota_verbatim: 200 GB for private models, alongside 200 GB for private datasets — from Kaggle's own product announcement 'Doubling of Private Quota and Public File Size Limit': 'Users now have a limit of 200GB for private models and 200GB for private datasets. Kaggle has also doubled the maximum upload size of public models and datasets from 100GB to 200GB.' Public models and public datasets have a 200 GB per-item ceiling and no published aggregate cap.
extras.limits_verbatim: per-object-cap 200 GB and 50 top-level files per dataset — 'A max of 50 top-level files (if you have more, use a directory structure and upload an archive)'. Uploading via the API is write-gated for most accounts. Practical caveat from the docs: archives are uncompressed server-side so their contents are usable in Notebooks, which means the 200 GB is measured on the expanded tree.
extras.egress_verbatim: Free — files come from Kaggle's Google-hosted CDN (storage.googleapis.com) with no egress meter. Downloads require a Kaggle API token.
extras.chaining_verbatim: Models and datasets are separate quota pools, so the ceiling is 200 GB private models + 200 GB private datasets + 200 GB per public model × N public models + 200 GB per public dataset × N public datasets. Public items are the real multiplier. Each model can carry multiple variations and frameworks, but they share the model's 200 GB.
extras.tooling_verbatim: kagglehub and the Kaggle API. Verified live this session: GET /api/v1/models/list?search=bert and ?search=qwen both returned 200 with real model records (ref, title, author, vote counts); GET /api/v1/models/google/bert/get returned 200, 72,158 bytes. Datasets: /api/v1/datasets/list returns 200 JSON with totalBytesNullable per dataset. Note the upload side is narrower than the read side — 'The ability to upload models via the Kaggle API was introduced to a select group of Kaggle accounts starting in version 1.5.18', and kagglehub caps at 50 files per repo and auto-zips beyond that.
extras.agent_focus: 2026-era research-data and data-marketplace platforms, deliberately judged on the BINDING constraint (does a person with only an email get past the write gate?) rather than on the marketing quota. Coverage: IEEE DataPort (the wave-7 discovery this slot confirms and extends), Mozilla Data Collective (2025 launch, the only new ≥100 GB-per-file free host found), Source Cooperative re-probed at the byte level, the French national Dataverse (Recherche Data Gouv) as the one genuinely EU-funded space with a self-serve email account, plus the 2026 data-marketplace entrants (Snowflake, Databricks Free Edition, data.world, Datarade, Tableland, Spice.ai, DataChain), the EU Data Spaces (Gaia-X / Catena-X / EOSC EU Node / DICE) and ResearchGate/Academia.edu data upload. Two structural results dominate: (a) the 'data marketplace' category is uniformly not storage — they are catalogues, and every one of them fails on per-object size by two to three orders of magnitude; (b) the EU Data Spaces are real and large but gated on eduGAIN/eIDAS identity, so they are closed on identity exactly like CSC Allas and LUMI-O before them.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
